\addlinespace[0.5pt]

Greedy accept length is 3.221 against 2.59 to 2.61 at temperature 0.7. The vendor reports 4.06 to 4.07 at four draft steps on benchmark text; ours is 2.83 at three on agent traffic. \textit{Source:} S s3, s4a; spec\_\allowbreak{}hist.py, spec\_\allowbreak{}greedy.py, read. \textit{Tier:} measured (ours); external (vendor). \textit{Hedge:} One unadjudicated run, counts only; greedy and sampled text differ. \\

\multicolumn{2}{@{}l}{\textbf{V3 trimtest: a paired decision test of leaner history}}\\*

\addlinespace[0.5pt]

\addlinespace[0.5pt]

Blind judge not run. 90\% state-bootstrap intervals. \textit{Source:} \texttt{\textasciitilde{}/\allowbreak{}.cache/\allowbreak{}arc3/\allowbreak{}trimtest-2026-10-20/\allowbreak{}trimtest\_\allowbreak{}replies.jsonl}; \texttt{solution/\allowbreak{}analysis/\allowbreak{}trim\_\allowbreak{}compare.py}, recomputed. \textit{Tier:} measured; moderate. \textit{Hedge:} The fail is on the point estimate; the interval contains the -0.05 tolerance. \\
\addlinespace[0.5pt]
V3-T4 & The difference is marginal as a test: paired per state (mean of the 4 cross pairs minus the full-full match), 24 states lower, 25 higher, 68 equal; a two-sided sign-flip permutation gives p = 0.093 (20,000 flips), consistent with the one-sided 95\% bound just below 0. \textit{Source:} v3\_\allowbreak{}board\_\allowbreak{}trim.py on the replies; \texttt{data/\allowbreak{}trimtest\_\allowbreak{}by\_\allowbreak{}state.csv}, recomputed. \textit{Tier:} derived; moderate. \textit{Hedge:} The gate was a tolerance rule, not a significance test; quote both. \\

Among replies that both act, agreement is 0.848 full-full (n 33) against 0.812 full-lean (n 133), post hoc. \textit{Source:} v3\_\allowbreak{}board\_\allowbreak{}trim.py (63 recomputed from \texttt{first\_\allowbreak{}action}); post-hoc figures from the gate record (read), source checked. \textit{Tier:} measured; moderate. \textit{Hedge:} The measured change is mainly acting sooner, not picking a different action; the gate counts both. \\

\addlinespace[0.5pt]

A one-hot chain drafter of 3 steps is capped near 1 + c + c\textsuperscript{2} + c\textsuperscript{3} = 3.500 accepted tokens per step (4.190 at 4 steps), against 2.830 live: headroom +0.670 (the D4 plan asked for +0.40). The ceiling idea is Bebop's (v2 E1). \\

V3-T8 & Parser defect, verdict unchanged: the gate's \texttt{first\_\allowbreak{}action} takes the first quoted identifier inside \texttt{action(}, which for the dict form \texttt{action([\{`action': `UP'\}, ...])} is the key, so 77 of 189 acting replies parse as ``ACTION'' whatever the move (43 more are variables, ``VAR''). Reading the dict value instead (61 of the 77 are MOUSE clicks) gives full-full 0.778, full-lean 0.697, difference -0.081 [-0.145, -0.015]: still a fail, slightly stronger. \textit{Source:} \texttt{paper/\allowbreak{}v3/\allowbreak{}analysis/\allowbreak{}v3\_\allowbreak{}trim\_\allowbreak{}parser.py} on the replies (new, post hoc), recomputed. \textit{Tier:} measured; moderate. \textit{Hedge:} Post hoc, not part of the gate. The action name ignores click coordinates, so MOUSE against MOUSE counts as agreement. \\

\multicolumn{2}{@{}l}{\textbf{V3 GRPO round A}}\\*
V3-G1 & \textbf{WA data.} 900 train windows came from 264 plays (200 R1, 64 replica). All are mixed-clear: 658 replica windows from the 8 public train-half games and 242 R1 windows from 11 RE-ARC-3 games. The set spans 19 games and 32 game-levels, with a top game-level share of 0.05. Positive share 0.581, net/\allowbreak{}gross advantage -0.197, mean abs advantage 0.374, 17.85M est tokens. 21 R1 plays were cut by the 280K cap, and the 17 bench games' plays (8 each) were skipped. Groups: R1 had 227 groups, of which 158 were skipped (reward range under 0.1), 3 had too few plays and 66 were kept (54 death-only, 12 mixed). The replicas had 53 groups: 23 skipped for range, 7 with too few plays, 23 kept (20 mixed, 3 death-only), 12 plays censored. Hashes: portable windows sha256 40ffa0b3...; trainer file d3660e4f...; images 19d05592... over 2,663 images. \textit{Source:} VM \texttt{\textasciitilde{}/\allowbreak{}arc3r2/\allowbreak{}wa/\allowbreak{}windows\_\allowbreak{}review.json}, \texttt{phase\_\allowbreak{}windows.log}; GATES.md data record; Vertex check in \texttt{gs:/\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}arc3-rep-uc1/\allowbreak{}grpo2/\allowbreak{}runs/\allowbreak{}wb/\allowbreak{}progress.txt} (``925 windows, 2663 images, 0 missing'', sha256 as expected), read. \textit{Tier:} measured; strong. \textit{Hedge:} The windows are the pin's own play. 27\% are RE-ARC-3, the family both r16 adapters drifted toward. \\
\addlinespace[0.5pt]
V3-G2 & \textbf{WC data.} 882 windows (858 mixed, 24 death-only), all from the 64 replica plays of the 8 public train games. 23 game-levels, top share 0.073, positive share 0.663, net/\allowbreak{}gross -0.031, mean abs advantage 0.291, 17.55M est tokens. Its 25 val windows are byte-identical to WA's. Hashes: portable sha256 6cb9eda3...; source 94238582... (equal to PARALLEL.md's \texttt{nor1t18.jsonl}); 2,356 images. \textit{Source:} VM \texttt{\textasciitilde{}/\allowbreak{}arc3r2/\allowbreak{}wc/\allowbreak{}prep.log}, \texttt{windows\_\allowbreak{}review.json}; GCS \texttt{runs/\allowbreak{}wc/\allowbreak{}progress.txt} (``907 windows, 2356 images, 0 missing''), read. \textit{Tier:} measured; strong. \textit{Hedge:} 8 games and 23 game-levels, so memorization would show only as no bench gain. \\
\addlinespace[0.5pt]
V3-G3 & \textbf{Recipe.} Reward per (play, level) is 1 if cleared within budget, minus 0.1 x min(deaths, 5). Advantage is (reward - group mean) x 2i/\allowbreak{}(n+1), with no supervision where abs A $<$ 0.05. Loss is the token mean over 16 windows of -sg(rho) A m log pi + 0.01 k3, where: rho = pi /\allowbreak{} pi\_\allowbreak{}old; pi\_\allowbreak{}old = the base, from a no-grad LoRA-off pass before each window; m = 0 outside [0.8, 1.28] or outside either keep set; log pi uses logits /\allowbreak{} 0.7 renormalized over SGLang's top-k 20 /\allowbreak{} top-p 0.95 keep set. Optimizer: AdamW at 3e-5, constant after 3 warmup steps, betas (0.9, 0.95), wd 0, clip 1.0; gnorm skip at 3x median. LoRA r16, alpha 16 (scale 1.0) on attention, GDN and the shared expert; routed experts and router frozen. One epoch is 57 steps for WA and WB, 56 for WC. Stops: val k3 $>$ 0.02 or entropy $>$ 10\%. Null below 0.002. T-kill at 90 GiB or under 550 tok/\allowbreak{}s. \textit{Source:} GATES.md ``Round A (WA)''; \texttt{train.py} \texttt{ra\_\allowbreak{}loss} (lines 120 to 136) and the loop (lines 300 to 390), code read; \texttt{args.txt} of runs wb and wc in GCS (the flags match GATES), read. \textit{Tier:} owner-reported (recipe); measured (code reading); strong. \textit{Hedge:} The band, beta and clip come from others' recipes (agent-factory-3, DAPO, GiGPO per DECISION.md); the thresholds are our judgment. \\
\addlinespace[0.5pt]
V3-G4 & \textbf{The defect.} At step 0 the adapter is zero, so the reading is base vs base. WA's first attempt read raw val k3 12.909 with k1 -0.0026, on 66,949 val tokens in 24 windows. One token moving ln(12.909 x 66,949) = 13.67 nats explains it. The predeclared stop (k3 $>$ 0.02) would have fired at step 8 with nothing kept. Raw step-0 k3 in the other base-vs-base readings: 0.1357 (WA), 0.1238 (WB), 0.1267 (WC), 23.14 (smoke). \textit{Source:} VM \texttt{wa/\allowbreak{}train.log.k3bug-1752}, \texttt{wa/\allowbreak{}train.log}; GCS \texttt{runs/\allowbreak{}\{wb,wc,trsmoke2\}/\allowbreak{}out/\allowbreak{}train.log}, read. \textit{Tier:} measured; strong. \textit{Hedge:} Raw k3 is unusable as a stop on this stack. It spans 0.12 to 23 for the same comparison. \\
\addlinespace[0.5pt]
V3-G5 & \textbf{Pass-to-pass noise, recomputed.} Five independent base passes of the same 24 val windows were compared: three VM processes (17:52Z, 17:55Z, the final WA run) and two Vertex hosts (WB, WC). Across all 10 pairs: only 12.1\% to 12.4\% of tokens match exactly; 45.7\% to 46.0\% differ by more than 0.01 nats; 16.9\% to 17.1\% leave the [0.8, 1.28] ratio band; 2.9\% to 3.1\% move more than 1 nat; 336 to 384 tokens move more than 2 nats. Max abs 7.0 to 18.4 nats, RMS 0.365 to 0.373 nats. Clipped k3 is 0.0629 to 0.0658 in both directions (mean 0.0644, SD 0.0008, n = 20), while raw k3 is 0.099 to 1,525. VM-VM, VM-Vertex and Vertex-Vertex pairs cannot be told apart. The within-run floors (0.0643, 0.0641, 0.0644, 0.0650; SD 0.0004) sit inside the same range. \textit{Source:} , recomputed. \textit{Tier:} measured; strong. \textit{Hedge:} Cause not identified. That routing or sparse-attention selection flips amplify over 20K-token windows is an inference we did not test. These are full-vocabulary log-probs at logits /\allowbreak{} 0.7 on the pin's own tokens. \\
\addlinespace[0.5pt]
V3-G6 & \textbf{Training-side floor.} At step 1 the adapter is still zero, and the grad pass and the no-grad pass disagree. Masked shares at that step: WA's first attempt 16.56\% (4.95\% keep-set misses, 11.61\% by the band); WA final 16.64\% (4.95\%, 11.68\%); WB on Vertex 16.33\% (11.34\% by the band). Training k3 reads 0.027 to 0.029. Smoke steps 1 to 3 on Vertex match WA's tokens (329,179, 314,062, 311,225), gnorm and peaks exactly, with loss within 0.0025. \textit{Source:} VM \texttt{wa/\allowbreak{}adapter.k3bug-1752/\allowbreak{}log.jsonl}, \texttt{wa/\allowbreak{}adapter/\allowbreak{}log.jsonl}; GCS \texttt{runs/\allowbreak{}wb/\allowbreak{}out/\allowbreak{}log.jsonl}, \texttt{runs/\allowbreak{}trsmoke2/\allowbreak{}out/\allowbreak{}train.log}, recomputed. \textit{Tier:} measured; strong. \textit{Hedge:} The ``two identical passes'' are one grad pass and one no-grad pass of the same weights, so this floor mixes nondeterminism with a code-path difference. Amendment 2's ``11.6\%'' is the first attempt (11.61\%); the restart reads 11.68\%. \\
\addlinespace[0.5pt]
V3-G7 & \textbf{The fix.} \texttt{-{}-k3-clip 2} clamps each token's log ratio to [-2, 2] in the val k3, so a 13.7-nat token adds (e\textsuperscript{2} - 3)/\allowbreak{}66,949 = 6.6e-5. Both stops and the null rule then read k3 minus step 0's clipped reading (the run's own floor F). This is amendment 2, which drops amendment 1's max(0.002, 2F) null. The loss's KL keeps raw d. Smoke check: clipped val k3 at steps 0 to 3 read 0.06497, 0.06556, 0.06556, 0.06545, a spread of 0.00059 against the 0.02 margin, across two Vertex hosts (a resume after step 1). Both amendments came after the first base-vs-base reading and before any trained-adapter reading. \textit{Source:} GATES.md amendments 1, 2 and family; \texttt{train.py} \texttt{kl\_\allowbreak{}to\_\allowbreak{}base} and \texttt{net\_\allowbreak{}k3}; GCS \texttt{trsmoke2/\allowbreak{}out/\allowbreak{}train.log} and \texttt{progress.txt} (two hosts), read. \textit{Tier:} owner-reported (rule); measured (spread); strong. \textit{Hedge:} The rule changed after seeing noise data, not signal. The floor's own SD (0.0008) is 40\% of the 0.002 null margin, so the null rule is near its noise. \\
\addlinespace[0.5pt]
V3-G8 & \textbf{WA curve.} Each reading gives net k3 /\allowbreak{} entropy /\allowbreak{} val NLL against step 0: step 8 +0.0001 /\allowbreak{} +1.6\% /\allowbreak{} +0.75\%; step 16 +0.0116 /\allowbreak{} +5.4\% /\allowbreak{} +1.86\%; step 24 +0.0260 /\allowbreak{} +11.1\% /\allowbreak{} +3.92\%. Step 24 broke both stops, and step 16 was selected (not null: 0.0116 $>$ 0.002). Run: 24 of 57 steps, 3.09 h, 878 tok/\allowbreak{}s, peak 87.05 GiB, 0 skipped steps, T-kills false. Selected sha256 fa80a6db... (equal to ckpt\_\allowbreak{}16), uploaded 21:06Z; md5 57e8a481... identical in both buckets. \textit{Source:} VM \texttt{wa/\allowbreak{}adapter/\allowbreak{}train\_\allowbreak{}summary.json}, \texttt{train.log}, \texttt{uploaded.md5}, \texttt{sha256sum} of selected and ckpt\_\allowbreak{}16; \texttt{gcloud storage ls -L} of both dataset copies, recomputed. \textit{Tier:} measured; strong (readings), weak (meaning). \textit{Hedge:} One seed. V3-G11 & \textbf{Drift tracks lr x steps.} WA at step 16 and WB at step 8 both reach lr x steps = 4.8e-4, and they read alike: net k3 0.0116 vs 0.0136, entropy +5.4\% vs +6.3\%, val NLL +1.86\% vs +1.82\%. V3-G12 & \textbf{Supervision mass is net negative.} net/\allowbreak{}gross advantage over in-band tokens is negative on 17 of 24 WA steps (median -0.42; 13 at -0.4 or below; range -0.85 to +0.55) and 11 of 16 WB steps (median -0.44). WC is 5 of 8 (median -0.06, mean +0.04). The window-level positive share is 0.581 for WA, so failed plays carry more tokens. Keep-set misses stay near 5.5\%. gnorm median 0.041 (WA), 0.047 (WB), 0.024 (WC); max 0.075; no step skipped. WA and WB tokens per step are equal at all 16 shared steps. \textit{Source:} , recomputed. \textit{Tier:} measured; strong. \textit{Hedge:} That negative-dominated updates raise entropy is an inference, not a test. val NLL rise equals k1 on the same tokens (WA at 24: dNLL 0.0272 vs k1 0.0283), so ``entropy and val NLL rising together'' is two readings, not three. \\
\addlinespace[0.5pt]
V3-G13 & \textbf{Gate (a') state.} 400 states from 136 request logs of the 17 bench games. Base and H have 800 replies each (0 errors, 4,022 s and 4,027 s). V3-W33 & Public harnesses and literature behind the replay check, verified against saved copies 2026-11-02. Twin (arXiv 2608.14490): 93.3 on the 25 public games with GPT-5.6 Sol; the ablation keeps the agent, model, file bridge and sandbox and disables the whole harness (executable world model, replay validation, exploration, planning, halt-on-mismatch executor) and scores 61.1, so the gap is not a replay-only effect; during the reported runs the goal check was asked for by prompt (its Appendix D); one scored run per game. Rodionov (arXiv 2607.15439): 4 nested variants by 4 model settings, one run each; the verification variant ranks first in every setting, margins 0.62 to 8.56 points over simplification; verification is prompted and tool-supported, not enforced, and the author does not separate it from the bundle. Kepler (arXiv 2610.00834): backtesting is instructed, not forced; the first mismatch voids the remaining plan. Tycho (arXiv 2607.28287): replays the latest attempt per level; route given as advice, no halting executor. arc-skill: every press needs a written prediction, plans halt at the first miss; the full-history rules check is optional. WorldCoder and PoE-World originate the program-world-model pattern (secondhand via Twin). Graph exploration (Rudakov et al., arXiv 2512.24156) reaches deep states at near-zero action efficiency per Twin. persistgym (arXiv 2610.26632): truncation costs little when facts can be re-observed. Rivals: no top-12 team published its changes after Franzen's notebook (read 2026-11-01); xz (rank 3) ported its solution to Kaggle 10-25, validates on public-25 and copycat-30, starts games at the 10-minute mark and RESETs every 7 minutes (forum 752485, 753843); Tufa reports scored notebooks lose about 40 minutes (forum 753843). Not verified: the digest's EMPA and AutumnBench specifics; Turducken's heal fine-tune and prompt claims (repo records only). \textit{Source:} Saved pages and full texts in the session scratchpad (pubharness/\allowbreak{}, pdfs/\allowbreak{}twin.txt, forum JSON); fact sheet copied to \texttt{docs/\allowbreak{}research/\allowbreak{}2026-11-01-harness/\allowbreak{}LITERATURE.md}; BibTeX in \texttt{paper/\allowbreak{}v3/\allowbreak{}tex/\allowbreak{}refs.bib}, read. \textit{Tier:} source-verified; strong for quoted numbers. \textit{Hedge:} Frontier-model magnitudes do not transfer to a 6B-active open model; every comparison above is one run per game or per setting. \\

Yield 2,048 (build l1a1y8sv2r3rqy2): yw-y2-c-1 123 (us-east4), c-3 125 (us-central1), c-4 119 (us-central1), e-2 124 (us-central1), e-3 123 (us-central1), e-4 125 (us-central1); mean 123.17, SD 2.23. Difference 8,192 minus 2,048: -2.50 levels, exact run-label permutation p 0.42, Welch p 0.41, run-bootstrap 95\% interval -7.5 to +2.5 (narrow by construction with six runs); by region -3.8 (us-central1) and +4.0 (us-east4); at matched tokens -3.17 (p 0.34); tokens per game 256.8K against 252.9K (+1.5\%); resume openers per game 8.97 against 26.95 (a third as many). Interval used in Figure 3 and the text: -2.50 plus or minus t(0.975, 6 df) x 8.25 x sqrt(2/\allowbreak{}6), with t 2.4469 and the six identical pairs' SD 8.25, the paper's convention for every interval at the pairs' SD: -14.2 to +9.2, so the test excludes the across-days +12.5 and any gain above about 9 levels, and does not exclude smaller gains; at the SD of the eight same-day runs, 5.95 (7 df, t 2.3646) it is -10.6 to +5.6. The two builds differ in one line of cell 7 (the yield token count); notebook sha256 prefixes a8e2e846639b (8,192) and e695102c96ba (2,048). The across-days comparison it was designed to settle carried 17\% more tokens in seven of nine treated runs, worth about 5 of the 12.5 levels at the curve's elasticity (D9), and was not interleaved (D8): drift and those tokens are candidate causes of the non-reproduction, and this test cannot apportion them. \textit{Source:} \texttt{paper/\allowbreak{}v3/\allowbreak{}analysis/\allowbreak{}out/\allowbreak{}yield\_\allowbreak{}wave/\allowbreak{}read\_\allowbreak{}2026-10-24.json} (per-run levels, tokens, region, validity; read by \texttt{paper/\allowbreak{}v3/\allowbreak{}analysis/\allowbreak{}yield\_\allowbreak{}wave\_\allowbreak{}read.py}); predeclared design \texttt{solution/\allowbreak{}kaggle/\allowbreak{}generated/\allowbreak{}gate-predeclared-2026-10-21-yield-interleaved.json} (declared\_\allowbreak{}at 2026-10-21 about 02:48Z, before the first submission at 02:49:55Z; decision rules amended 02:55Z while all 16 jobs were PENDING); \texttt{docs/\allowbreak{}PROGRESS.md} entries 2026-10-21 02:51Z, 06:45Z and 2026-10-24 04:00Z (launch, the four missing runs, the verdict); interval recomputed by \texttt{paper/\allowbreak{}v3/\allowbreak{}analysis/\allowbreak{}figs/\allowbreak{}fig\_\allowbreak{}yield.py} (asserted: -14.2 and +9.2), source checked. \textit{Tier:} measured (levels, tokens); derived (interval); strong. \textit{Hedge:} Six runs per arm, one build, Vertex AI Spot instances, regions not balanced after the four lost jobs; the design cannot show whether a resume changes decisions; the interval rules out gains above about 9 levels, not small ones; it ran on Vertex AI, not Kaggle. \\

One family draw reaches 40.98 with p 0.030 (z 1.88). Builds with 2 or more draws: within-build SD 2.77, ANOVA across builds F 2.34, p 0.113, between-build SD 2.08. r3p's three draws average 38.43; with reliability 0.63 the shrunk mean is 37.01, 2.4 above the family mean. Expected private score of the two auto-selected draws: between 34.59 and 37.01, per-draw SD 3.39. \textit{Source:} \texttt{paper/\allowbreak{}v3/\allowbreak{}analysis/\allowbreak{}v3\_\allowbreak{}gates\_\allowbreak{}board.py} and \texttt{out/\allowbreak{}gates\_\allowbreak{}board.json} and \texttt{.md}; \texttt{figs/\allowbreak{}data/\allowbreak{}board\_\allowbreak{}draws\_\allowbreak{}all\_\allowbreak{}2026-11-02.csv}, recomputed. \textit{Tier:} derived; moderate. \textit{Hedge:} The model choice moves P(best at least 40.98) between 0.17 and 0.64. Public and private halves hold different games; a game-split term is not estimable from these data. The family SD includes build differences. \\
\addlinespace[0.5pt]
V3-W53 & A second population, SWE-Bench-Verified. Bjarnason, Silva and Monperrus (arXiv 2602.07150) repeat 12 model, scaffold and temperature cells ten times each on 500 tasks: pass@1 SD 0.7 to 1.8 points (median 1.45) on means of 16.4\% to 63.8\%, relative SD 1.7\% to 8.1\%, against our 3.3\% to 7.2\% (SD 3.9 to 8.25 on 111 to 124 levels). The recipe MDE = 2.80 x SD x sqrt(2/\allowbreak{}n) gives 5.7 points at one run per arm (median SD; 2.8 to 7.1 across the range), 4.1 at two, 2.6 at five. Their abstract: standard deviations exceeding 1.5 points even at temperature 0, and 2.2 to 6.0 points depending on which run is picked. \textit{Source:} \texttt{paper/\allowbreak{}v3/\allowbreak{}analysis/\allowbreak{}v3\_\allowbreak{}second\_\allowbreak{}population.py} and \texttt{out/\allowbreak{}second\_\allowbreak{}population.json} and \texttt{.md}; Table 1 of the paper (HTML version) and abstract, read 2026-11-04, recomputed. \textit{Tier:} read (table), derived (MDE); moderate. \textit{Hedge:} Within-config SDs to which we applied our formula; nobody has tested the recipe's predictions there. The 2.2 to 6.0 is a spread over runs, not a measured gain. Not the same quantity as ours (a pass rate, not a weighted sum of all-or-nothing levels). \\
\addlinespace[0.5pt]
V3-W54 & Franzen-notebook copies, a cross-section rebuilt from two daily board snapshots (\texttt{daily/\allowbreak{}board-2026-10-01.csv} and \texttt{-10-02.csv}): teams whose submission count rose by exactly 1 and whose prior best was under a floor. Floor 10: 220 teams, mean 26.03, SD 3.67, median 26.22; floor 15: 215, 26.35, 3.04, 26.25; floor 20: 208, 26.63, 2.65, 26.38. Son Pham's forum post reports mean 25.77, SD 3.93, median 26.19 with n shown only in a screenshot (not stated in text; a request for n on 2026-10-06 has no reply in the stored dump). MDE at n = 1 for floor 15: 12.0 points. \textit{Source:} \texttt{out/\allowbreak{}second\_\allowbreak{}population.json}; \texttt{paper/\allowbreak{}v2/\allowbreak{}analysis/\allowbreak{}out/\allowbreak{}new\_\allowbreak{}repeat\_\allowbreak{}sets.json}; \texttt{paper/\allowbreak{}v2/\allowbreak{}evidence/\allowbreak{}board.md} line 58; bib key pham2026forum745062, recomputed. \textit{Tier:} measured; moderate. \textit{Hedge:} A cross-section of different teams (edits, hardware, failed runs included), not repeats of one build; `unchanged copy' is not checked per team; no team in the repository other than us has several scored draws of byte-identical code. Pham's n is unknown. \\
\addlinespace[0.5pt]
V3-W55 & Within-job ARC-AGI-3 repeat sets. Tufa Labs' example run in its public duck-harness repository (Qwen3.6-27B FP8, 25 public games, 20 passes in one job): 17, 15, 17, 21, 16, 16, 15, 13, 10, 13, 19, 17, 18, 14, 15, 14, 16, 14, 16, 13 levels, mean 15.45, SD 2.44 (relative SD 15.8\%; MDE at one run per arm 9.7 levels). Franzen's v3 notebook output, 4 passes in one job: 102, 106, 104, 105 levels, mean 104.25, SD 1.71 (MDE at one run per arm 6.8). \textit{Source:} \texttt{out/\allowbreak{}second\_\allowbreak{}population.json} and \texttt{paper/\allowbreak{}v2/\allowbreak{}analysis/\allowbreak{}out/\allowbreak{}new\_\allowbreak{}repeat\_\allowbreak{}sets.json} (tufa, franzen\_\allowbreak{}v3; Tufa file benchmark.json at commit 41548cadbf, pushed 2026-07-01), recomputed. \textit{Tier:} measured; moderate. \textit{Hedge:} Both are within one job, so they contain no session-to-session shift and neither confirms nor refutes 8.25 or 5.6 about the shift; a different model and scale in Tufa's case. \\
\addlinespace[0.5pt]
V3-W56 & The interleaved yield test, intervals and the size of the non-reproduction. Difference 8,192 minus 2,048 is -2.50 (six runs per arm); 95\% interval -14.15 to +9.15 at the pairs' SD 8.25 (t on 6 df; the widest, the paper's convention), -10.62 to +5.62 at 5.95 (7 df), -8.78 to +3.78 at the test's own pooled within-arm SD 4.88 (10 df). Across days (nine runs of the 8,192 family against 21 controls) the gap is +12.52, z 3.8 at SD 8.25 and 5.3 at 5.95. Across-days gap minus interleaved difference = 15.02; its SE is 5.79 at SD 8.25 (z 2.6) and 4.17 at 5.95 (z 3.6), from SE = SD x sqrt(1/\allowbreak{}9 + 1/\allowbreak{}21 + 1/\allowbreak{}6 + 1/\allowbreak{}6). \textit{Source:} \texttt{out/\allowbreak{}variance\_\allowbreak{}frames.json} (yield\_\allowbreak{}test\_\allowbreak{}interval\_\allowbreak{}by\_\allowbreak{}sd); V3-W36; D1, recomputed. \textit{Tier:} derived; moderate. \textit{Hedge:} Normal approximation; arms are not interleaved across days, so the 15.0 mixes drift, build and tokens; seven of the nine across-days runs carry other serving changes. `Run noise alone cannot explain the shortfall' is the reading of a z of 2.6 or more. \\
\addlinespace[0.5pt]
V3-W57 & The easy-data rate behind the fine-tuning reading. The agent clears 548 of 601 RE-ARC-3 levels (91.2\%) counted as the best per game over three attempts merged across Spot attempts (V3-L1); in one play on the public 25 the same pin clears 124.0 of 183 levels (67.8\%, 68\%). \textit{Source:} V3-L1; V3-W3; V3-W9 (124.4 mean of 18 runs), read. \textit{Tier:} derived; moderate. \textit{Hedge:} The two rates differ in kind (best of three attempts against one play), so 91\% against 68\% overstates the gap in difficulty; it is a reading, not a measurement. \\
\addlinespace[0.5pt]
V3-W58 & The fail-closed hedge. The 2026-10-18 draw (submission \subid{57343805}, hm32p, 0.00, 3,411 bytes) was submitted at the 06:56Z catch-up after two missed fires. Its build, hm32p, is r3p plus a draft vocabulary map, and r3p carries both fail-closed checks (server exit before READY; under 20 levels at the end), so the checks were present and did not stop a banked 0.00; the cause is unknown. Neither check has fired on a scored run, and a run Kaggle kills from outside is not caught. \textit{Source:} \texttt{CLAUDE.md} (pinned-config paragraph: r3p components, hm32p), \texttt{docs/\allowbreak{}STATE.md}, \texttt{board\_\allowbreak{}draws.csv}; V3-B7; B10, read. \textit{Tier:} owner-reported; moderate. \textit{Hedge:} A scored run returns no log, so whether the run died before READY, after 20 levels or by outside kill is not known; only that the checks did not turn it into an error. \\
